_meta.purpose: Per-section expected wall-clock durations for test/watchdog.py. A section is EITHER a JS jsMark() label (test/selftest.js, tag "js") or a module SelfTestSectionMark() label (src/module/*.cpp, tag "module"). Two independent timing files carry these live -- $PICOPILOT_SELFTEST_JS_TIMINGS and $PICOPILOT_SELFTEST_SECTION_TIMINGS -- see SelfTestTiming.h and selftest.js's jsMark().
_meta.generated_from: a full green-ish run captured 2026-09-26 (thist-hang-investigation scratchpad, runs/s87-11.log, main-checkout build near commit 9c06ebf0) -- real measured durations, not guesses.
_meta.cap_formula: Unless a section below carries an explicit "cap" (seconds), watchdog.py computes cap = max(floor_seconds, baseline * multiplier). floor_seconds and multiplier default to 60 and 5 (override: --floor/--multiplier or PICOPILOT_WATCHDOG_FLOOR_S/PICOPILOT_WATCHDOG_MULTIPLIER). A section with NO entry here at all gets --default-cap (default 90s, env PICOPILOT_WATCHDOG_DEFAULT_CAP_S).
_meta.explicit_cap_sections: The two GraXpert-core lock waits (B10 live / B10b stand-in) are pinned to their own PixInsight-core external-program lock timeout (GraXpertCoreSelfTestLock, PICopilotInc5SelfTest.cpp: coreLock(300)) plus margin, NOT to baseline*multiplier -- under multi-agent load one run can legitimately queue behind another's GraXpert-core call for up to 300s, and 5x the observed baseline (a handful of seconds, taken on an uncontended box) would false-trigger the watchdog on ordinary contention.
